## Notes

Read more about hairy plots, and how this one was made, in the blog post [The Hairy Chart](../).

::: {.ha-callout data-series="target"}
**Federal Funds Target Rate.** The rate the Federal Open Market Committee announces it is aiming for. A single number until December 2008, a quarter-point range from then on; the line marks the middle of the range.
:::

::: {.ha-callout data-series="treasury_forward"}
**Treasury Forward Curve.** What the Treasury bond market implies about future short rates, backed out daily by Federal Reserve Board staff from a smooth curve fitted across the whole maturity spectrum. A forward rate is the expected future short rate plus a term premium, so it is not a pure expectation. One hair per FOMC meeting, since 1994.
:::

::: {.ha-callout data-series="options_implied"}
**Options-Implied (SOFR).** What options traders are collectively betting, as a full probability distribution over where the overnight rate will average in a future three-month window. Each hair is the mean for each upcoming window, as of one day. Daily since March 2023.
:::

::: {.ha-callout data-series="sep_median"}
**FOMC Median Projection.** Four times a year each of the Federal Reserve's senior policymakers writes down where they think the federal funds rate *should* be at the end of each of the next few years. This is the middle answer, published since September 2015.
:::

::: {.ha-callout data-series="spf_median"}
**Professional Forecasters.** Every quarter the Philadelphia Fed asks a few dozen professional forecasters where the three-month Treasury bill rate will be over the next five quarters, and publishes the median. The bill normally sits a little below fed funds, so a forecast of the bill rate works as a rough forecast of the policy rate that runs slightly low. 
:::

::: {.ha-callout data-series="recessions"}
**Recessions.** US recessions, shaded from the business cycle peak to the trough, using the turning points determined by the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER).
:::

Each hair starts on the target line at the date its forecast was made, and runs from there to the source's first forecast.

The [R notebook](../r/) and the [Python notebook](../python/) walk through how to access the data and build each series, with each publisher's own description and links to the source data.
